learning_units.description: Tokka clapper beat coordination with step movement.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Hand mudras mimicking natural elements; waving colorful scarves; balancing lamps on hands; striking bamboo clappers.
movement_profile.footwork: Progressive village-to-village walking steps that build in tempo; localized lower-body swaying and stepping.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Processions moving across village terrain; small group floor patterns of 4 to 6 members.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Isolated lower-body motion in Hojagiri while torso remains stationary to support head props; fluid natural torso sways in Lebang Boomani.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily grounded stepping and swaying; minimal high jumping.
movement_profile.partnering: Complementary gender roles where men manage rhythm instruments/clappers and women perform prop/scarf movement.
movement_profile.posture: Varies from erect torso holding balance with lower-body isolation (Hojagiri) to fluid, bending stances mimicking agricultural acts and nature (Lebang Boomani, Mosak sulmani).

signature_moves.description: Men striking bamboo clappers rhythmically to attract insects.
signature_moves.name: Tokka Clapping

signature_moves.description: Women waving bright scarves through the air to catch flying insects.
signature_moves.name: Lebang Scarf Catch

signature_moves.description: Reang women swaying hips and moving lower body while balancing bottles, pitchers, or lamps.
signature_moves.name: Prop Balancing Lower Isolation

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Accelerating from a steady initial tempo to a fast peak.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid sudden head movements during balancing routines; do not disassociate upper and lower body isolations during prop balancing.

music_profile.musical_form: Strophic rhythmic framework that gradually accelerates in tempo.
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Rhythmic bamboo clapper striking (tokka) coupled with steady khamb and pung percussion beats that accelerate progressively.
music_profile.sound_description: A vibrant acoustic blend dominated by the sharp, repetitive crack of bamboo tokka clappers, deep resonant thuds of khamb and pung percussion, melismatically floating bamboo flute melodies, and high-pitched sarinda strings.
music_profile.vocal_style: Group unison singing by team members accompanying performance.

basic_steps: Gradual tempo shift from slow step-touch to rapid rhythmic footwork (Goria)
Tokka bamboo clapper striking pattern by male dancers (Lebang Boomani)
Scarf waving in rhythmic sweeping paths to capture imaginary insects (Lebang Boomani)
Lower-body isolated hip and sway movements while keeping the upper torso rigid and balancing head props (Hojagiri)
teaching.formation: Mixed-gender lines or processional groups moving village to village (Goria); teams of 4 to 6 women (Hojagiri); paired gender groups (Lebang Boomani).
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic step patterns and clapper rhythms of Lebang Boomani or Goria before attempting lower-body isolation and object balancing in Hojagiri.
teaching.rhythm: Varies by form; driven by khamb drums, pung percussion, bamboo clappers, and flutes with gradually increasing tempo.
